questions.prompt: What is the best senior framing for pyproject.toml in a modern Python project?

options.label: It is a project metadata and tool configuration surface, not the whole reproducibility story.
It is always a lockfile equivalent to package-lock.json.
It is only useful for libraries and should be avoided in services.

questions.explanation: pyproject.toml centralizes metadata and tool configuration, while reproducible installs still need a clear locking or deployment contract.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap with the isolation mechanism Python teams normally use for project installs.
questions.template: A {{blank}} keeps project dependencies from bleeding into the global Python installation.
questions.explanation: Virtual environments isolate installed packages for local and service workflows.

questions.prompt: Order the packaging review questions from project contract to deployment reproducibility.

items.label: Separate runtime, optional, and development dependencies
Make the resolved dependency graph reproducible
Run CI and deployment from the same contract

questions.explanation: Version support, dependency intent, resolution, and CI enforcement are separate review concerns.

questions.prompt: Match each pyproject.toml area to its main purpose.
questions.explanation: Keeping these tables conceptually separate makes packaging reviews less tool-driven and more contract-driven.

questions.prompt: Why can Python package installs confuse JavaScript developers during onboarding?

options.label: Distribution names and import names always match exactly.
The installed distribution name and the import name can differ.
Python packages cannot expose importable modules.

questions.explanation: A distribution can expose a different import name, so project metadata and docs matter during setup.

questions.prompt: Match the packaging smell to the production risk.

pairs.match: standard library module can be shadowed

questions.explanation: Packaging problems often look like environment mysteries until the repo contract is explicit.

questions.prompt: A repo adopts src/ layout, but tests pass only because PYTHONPATH is hand-set locally. What should review ask for?

options.label: Keep the manual PYTHONPATH step because src/ layout always requires it.
Use a documented install or editable-install command that matches CI behavior.
Remove all __init__.py files so imports become automatic.

questions.explanation: The src/ layout is useful when installation behavior is explicit. Hidden path tweaks make local behavior diverge from production.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap for what a lockfile is meant to make reproducible.
questions.template: A useful Python lock process makes the resolved {{blank}} consistent across local, CI, and deployment.
questions.explanation: The lockfile matters only if the install commands actually use it across environments.

questions.prompt: Order the senior triage flow when an import works locally but fails in deployment.

items.label: Confirm the process uses the intended virtual environment
Check distribution name versus import name
Look for local modules shadowing dependencies
Align the install command with CI and deployment

questions.explanation: Import failures are often environment contract failures, not reasons to patch sys.path blindly.

which importable entry point starts the command

questions.explanation: Packaging review is about making environment and artifact assumptions explicit enough for CI and production.
